summary:
Anthony Sousa is a Canadian Liberal politician who has represented Mississauga—Lakeshore in the House of Commons since winning a 2022 by-election. He served as Ontario’s finance minister from 2013 to 2018 after representing Mississauga South in the provincial legislature from 2007.

The son of Portuguese immigrants, Sousa grew up in Mississauga, earned business degrees from Wilfrid Laurier University and the University of Western Ontario, and worked in banking for more than 20 years. In Ontario’s cabinet, he also served as labour minister and citizenship and immigration minister. As finance minister, he introduced the province’s first balanced budget since the 2008 recession, supported an enhanced Canada Pension Plan, and oversaw plans for major infrastructure investment. Ontario’s net debt rose from $252.1 billion to $305.2 billion during his time in the role.

Sousa lost his provincial seat in 2018. In September 2023, he became parliamentary secretary to the federal Minister of Public Services and Procurement. Re-elected in 2025, he became chair of the House of Commons Standing Committee on National Defence.
